title: Reusable Data Procedures
purpose: Turn repeated spreadsheet and corporate-export work into explicit, testable, versioned procedures that can be found, composed, governed and reused when source files change.
thesis: Discovery may use heuristics and AI assistance; approved procedures execute deterministically, preserve evidence and remain discoverable through a governed catalog.

workspace_contract.principle: Workspace responsibilities are stable even when folders are implemented as SharePoint locations, object-storage prefixes or service resources.

areas.Staging: Run-specific technical copies and conversions that can be rebuilt.
areas.Quarantine: Unreadable, ambiguous or unsafe sources that require review.
areas.Reference: Controlled dictionaries, code lists, lookup files and approved mappings.
areas.Work: Intermediate artifacts used for execution or debugging.
areas.Outbox: Published result and exception artifacts from successful or policy-approved runs.
areas.Evidence: Run manifest, hashes, profiles, drift, validations, exceptions and procedure version.
areas.Archive: Optional retained run packages or manifests according to data policy.

rules: Do not modify Inbox sources in place.
Every run has a unique run identifier.
Temporary work is reproducible from source plus procedure.
Failed or review-required runs do not silently publish to Outbox.
Evidence retention follows data classification and retention policy.

pipeline.purpose: Register files, hashes, arrival metadata and source-role candidates.
pipeline.gate: Source is readable and allowed for processing.

pipeline.purpose: Read file and workbook structure before reading all business rows.
pipeline.gate: Workbook or file structure is understood enough to continue.

pipeline.purpose: Find the intended table or region using stable evidence rather than fixed coordinates alone.
pipeline.gate: One source region has sufficient locator evidence.

pipeline.purpose: Convert the selected region into a logical table with traceable source positions.
pipeline.gate: Required fields and region shape are plausible.

pipeline.purpose: Create controlled canonical representations without hiding raw source evidence.
pipeline.gate: Critical parse and normalization rules satisfy policy.

pipeline.purpose: Resolve mappings, keys and lookup relationships with explicit cardinality.
pipeline.gate: Relation coverage and ambiguity are acceptable.
Transformation graph completes without unhandled errors.

pipeline.purpose: Check schema, data quality, relations, reconciliation controls and business invariants.
pipeline.gate: Validation severity is within publication policy.

pipeline.purpose: Produce result, exceptions and evidence artifacts.
Turn confirmed manual fixes into rules, references, aliases, reusable blocks or a proposed procedure revision.
pipeline.gate: Approved versions are never silently mutated.

design_principles: Capture intent and data logic rather than recorded UI actions.
Separate probabilistic discovery from deterministic execution.
Preserve raw source evidence before cleaning or transformation.
Separate representation cleanup from business-value changes.
Treat mapping suggestions as hypotheses with decomposed evidence.
Model drift, quarantine and repair as normal lifecycle behavior.
Keep procedure definitions portable across CLI, API, UI and agent clients.
Version behavior-changing procedure edits and preserve provenance.
Treat exceptions as first-class output data rather than console noise.
Catalog reusable capabilities by metadata instead of relying on folder names.
Promote repeated logic into typed versioned blocks.
Scale governance with criticality and data risk.

catalog.purpose: Make procedures and reusable assets findable, comparable, trustworthy and impact-aware.
search_examples: procedures affected by a reference dataset change
procedures allowed to run without AI or external network access
procedures with similar source contracts and mappings
catalog.rule: Run history is not the catalog. The catalog describes reusable assets; run evidence describes executions.

asset_types.block: Typed reusable capability with parameters, tests, owner and version.
asset_types.pattern: Recommended arrangement of blocks for a common problem.
asset_types.procedure: End-to-end business task with source and output contracts.
asset_types.pack: Curated domain bundle of procedures, blocks, references, fixtures and guidance.

rules: Approved procedures pin compatible block versions instead of resolving latest at runtime.
Prefer deterministic and side-effect-free blocks where practical.
Declare filesystem, network, reference-data and external-service side effects.
Custom code is an explicit escape hatch with tests, ownership and risk classification.
Review repeated implementation for promotion into a shared block, but avoid trivial over-fragmentation.

governance.principle: Govern reusable assets according to impact, criticality and data risk rather than applying the same process to every task.

change_rules.minor: Compatible alias, optional field or non-breaking validation with regression tests.
change_rules.major: Required source, key, mapping cardinality, business transform, output contract or incompatible shared-block change.

promotion_rules: Production execution uses approved procedure versions and pinned dependencies.
Promotion moves definitions and approved dependencies, not uncontrolled raw input data.
Major shared dependency changes require catalog impact analysis.
New custom code, external endpoints or AI data modes trigger policy review according to classification.
expiry_and_deprecation: Set review dates based on criticality.
Mark stale trust evidence without deleting historical catalog records.
Deprecated procedures point to a replacement when one exists.
Keep approved previous versions addressable for rollback and audit.

excel_discovery.rule: Store locator strategy, evidence and fallbacks, not only the coordinates found in one run.

layers.raw: Original source representation kept for traceability where required.
layers.canonical: Stable representation used for comparison, parsing and joins.
layers.business: Value changed by an explicit approved business rule.

rules: Never treat zero as null without an explicit rule.
Do not invent precision or digits already lost in the source.
Keep failed parse values as exceptions with raw value and rule ID.
Use symmetric normalization on both sides of joins.
Safe cleanup should normally be idempotent.

classes.compatible: The procedure can continue and records the difference.
classes.resolvable: A known repair such as an approved alias or moved region can be proposed.
classes.breaking: Execution stops because a required structural or relation assumption is no longer safe.
classes.business: Technical structure may match while the business meaning or policy has changed.

drift.rule: A repair creates a proposed procedure revision; it does not silently mutate an approved version.

field_techniques: Use at least several real files before calling a source pattern stable.
Prefer source roles and structural fingerprints over filenames alone.
Keep source sheet, row and column coordinates for rejected values.
Give every exception a reusable reason code.
Use cheap canary checks before expensive transformations.
Measure manual-touch rate and repeated exception rate.
Promote repeated manual fixes into rules, reference data or reusable blocks.
Report mapping coverage together with business impact where possible.

architecture.recommended_start: Python package plus CLI plus JSON procedure schema and Git-backed catalog metadata

ai_assistance.boundary: Accepted AI suggestions are compiled into explicit normal procedure logic. Repeated execution does not depend on free-form model reasoning.

roadmap.name: framework-and-cases
roadmap.goal: Stabilize workspace, pipeline, locator, cleaning, validation, catalog and procedure vocabulary against realistic repeated data-work cases.

roadmap.name: local-runtime
roadmap.goal: Implement deterministic Python runtime, Inbox workflow, CLI, run reports, registry metadata and regression fixtures.

roadmap.name: discovery-and-drift
roadmap.goal: Add workbook inspection, region location, profiling, mapping evidence, source matching and controlled repair.

roadmap.name: catalog-and-composition
roadmap.goal: Add reusable block library, dependency graph, search facets, packs and impact analysis.

roadmap.name: shared-service
roadmap.goal: Add registry API, review-oriented UI, scheduling and team environments around the same core engine.

roadmap.name: enterprise-controls
roadmap.goal: Add security profiles, approval policy, audit, observability, deprecation and enterprise source adapters.

roadmap.name: ai-assistance
roadmap.goal: Add controlled semantic assistance and retrieval of approved mappings, blocks and procedures.
